opener: Hi, this is Mia from ParcelGo customer support (case #77341). I'm reaching out because we attempted delivery at your address twice this week and no one was home. We hold packages for 5 days before returning them. Is this still a good address for you?

stages.name: hook
stages.llmGuidance: You're a helpful ParcelGo rep named Mia. Be friendly and conversational, not robotic. You have case #77341. Act like you genuinely want to help resolve the delivery. No link yet.
stages.scriptedFallback: Thanks for responding! Let me pull up your case. Can you confirm the last 4 digits of the phone number on the order?

stages.name: engage
stages.llmGuidance: Build trust by asking for a small piece of info (last 4 of phone on order). Sound helpful. Then mention you can process a one-time redirect to a ParcelGo pickup locker if they prefer.
stages.scriptedFallback: Got it! I can reroute this to a nearby pickup locker. I just need to verify your identity with the last 4 of your ZIP code.

stages.name: escalate
stages.llmGuidance: Mention there's a $4.95 locker transfer fee (waivable if they verify identity quickly). Create soft urgency — the 5-day hold expires tomorrow.
stages.scriptedFallback: The hold expires tomorrow at midnight. I can waive the $4.95 locker fee if you complete verification today: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: ask
stages.llmGuidance: Ask them to click the link and enter their name, ZIP, and card to confirm the pickup. Reassure them ParcelGo uses bank-level encryption.
stages.scriptedFallback: Here's your verification link: {{PRACTICE_LINK}} — just your name, ZIP, and card. We use bank-level encryption.

stages.name: reveal
stages.scriptedFallback: 🛑 PRACTICE SCAM — This was a Safe Signal exercise. Real ParcelGo reps never ask for card details over text.

hook.explanation: Scammers use friendly, conversational tone to seem legitimate
Real carrier support typically contacts you through the app or confirmed email

engage.explanation: Asking for 'last 4 of ZIP' or similar partial info is a trust-building step before bigger asks

escalate.explanation: Expiry tomorrow is a pressure tactic
Transfer fees collected over text are not how carriers operate

ask.explanation: No carrier collects card details via SMS link
Invoking 'bank-level encryption' is a trust signal scammers borrow to seem legitimate
